questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Many universities have a limited supply of courses taught in English. In Amsterdam, I was sure that they were good at speaking English, making it a safe choice with regards to the courses at the university.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy. You receive emails about every action you have to do. There is a very helpful exchange office at UvA that you can ask anything if you need help.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Again, the exchange office was very helpful. They could either provide the help themself or guide you to the correct place for help.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
The university is able to help most of the exchange students to find housing - I only met one or two other exchange students who didn't get housing through the university. 
You have to be aware of the dates when applying for housing through the university. After applying, you get a lottery number that tells how good are your chances at getting accommodation. Make sure to check your email regularly as there are many deadlines during this process. But it is worth all of the work, as it is very hard to find housing on your own in Amsterdam (especially when you don't live in Amsterdam when you are looking for housing there).

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: There is no on campus housing. Most of the student accommodations are located quite far from the city centre. I had to bike about 7 km to university (I lived at Fraijlemaborg). Besides the location, Fraijlemaborg was a very good student housing. They have studios where you can live on your own or apartments where you live with 1 or 2 other exchange students. I lived with two roomies and really enjoyed it - they ended up being some of my best friends in the city.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You received emails with good descriptions on what to do next. The deadlines were clearly indicated.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The exchange office at UvA was very helpful.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: It was very easy. UvA sent a list that I had to fill within a week. I chose to change one course during my exchange, but that wasn't a problem at all.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Just make sure to check your email and follow the deadlines, then everything is quite easy.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer:
The master at UvA is only one year, so it was quite intense being there for the first half year of their entire master. There's a lot of group work, and many presentations (compared to University of Copenhagen) which are there to make sure you work during the semester and not just before the exam. This can be a little stressful as an exchange student, as I didn't care about getting good grades, but just wanted to pass the courses. But it is a policy of the university so there's not a lot to do about it.
With that being said, I think the teachers at UvA were really good and the quality of the courses was quite high (about the same as at UCPH).

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: A lot of group work and presentations at UvA.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Macroeconomics, Microeconomics and Game Theory, International Economic Cooperation, Behavioral Economics, Public Economics, Climate Change Economics.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: In general, the teachers at UvA are really good and motivated. I especially enjoyed the courses: Behavioral Economics, Public Economics, and Climate Change Economics. These are some topics that I find very interesting.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Not really any. But you have to be aware that you have to pay quite a large deposit in advance of getting your student housing (around 10,000 DKK + 1,5 months of rent).

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: The supermarket and restaurants are a bit cheaper than Denmark. The public transport is based on how many km you travel. Since I lived a little outside the city, I think it was a little expensive to travel with public transport to the city. Most of the time, I used my bike that I rented at Swapfiets.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The only thing I participated in was a bouldering course through the university sports association - this was really nice!

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: A lot, but I didn't participate in much.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Try to join one of the sports courses that they have. It's quite cheap, a fun way to try a new sport and meet new people.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Enjoy the city, but also try to take daytrips to other parts of the country.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy. The Dutch are quite similar to the Danish.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Not really any.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: They are very open compared to Danes. It's easy to start a conversation with a stranger (also because everyone is really good at English).

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Don't know

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Not really.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Experiencing being "all alone" in a different country. It is not as hard as one could fear. It is a fun challenge and you realize that everything will be alright in the end.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Same as above.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
